answer: The network caps how much any single account can take per epoch, so even a cleverly large farm cannot monopolize one epoch's rewards — the surplus is spread across many passing identities. Consequently, an attacker with a large flock pays more to keep it alive than it can ever extract, which is why Sybil campaigns fail here.. This matters because the cost of running many aliases grows faster than the influence they can exert, making the attack economically self-defeating. Consider a umber as the anchor of the cost.
